html:
ForgeMCP bridge protocol 1

The editor adapters use their own small local protocol; the external server translates MCP calls into it. Only the Python server speaks MCP. No Codex-specific logic is built into either application adapter.

Registration fields: protocol_version: 1, session_id, kind (unreal or blender), host: "127.0.0.1", integer port, integer pid, and a random session token. Session registrations are runtime secrets, excluded from Git, MCP results, and logs. An application owns its registration file and removes it on normal shutdown. Version 0.1.2 protects Windows registration directories and files with an owner-and-SYSTEM-only DACL before advertising a session; protection failures prevent startup. Tokens use cryptographic randomness and rotate on bridge startup.

The server rediscovers registrations for each operation. forge_ensure_connected checks for exactly one responsive Unreal bridge and one responsive Blender bridge using authenticated health requests, then returns the selected session IDs. Optional explicit IDs resolve a selection when multiple sessions respond. Ambiguous sessions are not guessed. The call verifies reachability but does not keep a socket open or launch an application; a missing bridge must be started in Unreal or Blender.

A connection carries one UTF-8 JSON object terminated by a newline:

{"protocol_version":1,"request_id":"unique-id","token":"[redacted]","command":"health","args":{}}

Success:

{"request_id":"unique-id","ok":true,"data":{"read_only":true}}

Failure:

{"request_id":"unique-id","ok":false,"error":{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Session authentication failed."}}

Malformed JSON has no recoverable correlation ID. The server rejects missing or mismatched response IDs. Foundation commands are Unreal health, project_info, list_actors, editor_log, and capture_screenshot, and Blender health, scene_info. capture_screenshot returns a bounded JPEG of the active Unreal Editor viewport as an MCP image. The adapter reads current viewport pixels, scales them in memory to at most 1280x720, and never resizes the Editor window or writes a screenshot file. Unreal actor limit is an integer from 1 to 1000; its result includes total_count and truncated. The current editor world is inspected, including loaded actors; unloaded World Partition content is not enumerated. Blender reports fps, fps_base, and effective_fps separately.

Adapters cap requests at 16 KiB and 16 concurrent clients, with a ten-second client lifetime. The core caps responses at 1 MiB, with a ten-second inspection exchange timeout and sixty-second apply timeout. Outbound client lifetime resets after native execution so a completed compilation can send its response. JSON nesting is limited to eight containers and args, when supplied, must be an object. Excessively large input closes the connection. The Python core rejects linked/out-of-root registrations and does not reflect adapter-supplied error messages. Sockets are nonblocking on application threads; partially received requests and partially sent responses are buffered. There is no eval, arbitrary script execution, unrestricted filesystem write, or asset import endpoint.

Version 0.2.0 adds Unreal class_info, blueprint_info, blueprint_preview, and blueprint_apply, and Blender object_info, scene_preview, and scene_apply. Preview arguments contain a typed recipe. Apply arguments contain preview_id and matching confirmation. Previews are session-local, expire after ten minutes, and are consumed once. Apply returns an explicit operation state (completed, rolled_back, or partial); ok: true means a valid adapter response and must not be substituted for checking that state. Blueprint save and placement are explicit recipe flags. Blender recipes do not save the file. See Engineering.md [not indexed].

The development registry also exposes Unreal gas_info for bounded read-only GAS state inspection on one exact actor path in the idle editor world. The Blender scene recipe allowlist includes reviewed pose-bone keyframes; neither operation executes arbitrary application scripts.

Static-mesh transfer adapters expose read-only binding_info in Blender and mesh_binding_info in Unreal. These return stable current-content revisions and, where a transfer baseline is present, its binding ID and baseline fingerprints. The external MCP server combines those results as forge_compare_mesh_binding; comparison is inspection only and never applies a transfer.

Error codes include invalid_request, invalid_arguments, unauthorized, command_not_allowed, editor_not_ready, scene_not_ready, inspection_failed, session_not_found, ambiguous_session, disconnected, timeout, and invalid_response. A disconnected registration does not prove its application is currently running. Listing sessions performs an authenticated health check. Engineering errors also include invalid_recipe, confirmation_required, preview_not_found, stale_preview, preview_limit, invalid_context, asset_not_found, class_not_found, and object_not_found. Apply timeouts report outcome_unknown; inspect state before retrying.

See Security.md [not indexed] for threat boundaries and update activation.

Static mesh export stage

The Blender native allowlist additionally supports export_preview with exactly {"name": "SourceMesh"} and export_apply with exactly preview_id and confirmation, both equal to the reviewed export preview ID for apply. Every request still requires the session token and protocol envelope. No caller-selected filesystem path is accepted. Previews expire after 300 seconds and are single use.

Exports write a new binary FBX beneath the configured session directory's transfers/<blender-session>/<preview-id>/ directory. Preview writes no artifacts. Source geometry, mesh attributes, transform, units and material changes invalidate the preview. Existing staging directories are never overwritten. Export records are written before native export and updated atomically afterward; a retained export_started record requires inspection rather than blind retry.

An exported response establishes only the export stage. Unreal import, scene placement and downstream material/coordinate verification require separate native responses. Standalone blender_preview_export and blender_apply_export MCP tools expose this stage. The connected transfer tools below orchestrate native import and placement separately.

Staged Unreal static mesh import

The Unreal native allowlist supports mesh_import_preview with exactly one recipe object. Its required fields are transfer_id (32 lowercase hex digits), artifact_sha256 (64 lowercase hex digits), artifact_bytes (integer, 23 bytes to 64 MiB), asset_path (new /Game/ package), target_project_file (matching absolute project path), and target_session_id (matching editor PID session). Optional save is a Boolean and defaults to false. Unknown fields and incorrect JSON types are rejected. No caller-selected source file path is accepted.

The server's staging helper writes the checked artifact as <project>/Saved/ForgeTransfers/<transfer_id>/mesh.fbx, alongside its manifest and staging record. Preview verifies the file's path, header, size and checksum and rejects existing destination assets or import recovery records. Previews expire after 300 seconds, with at most 32 pending previews per bridge.

mesh_import_apply accepts exactly preview_id and equal confirmation. It consumes the preview, repeats project/session/world/file validation, locks the Windows artifact against writes and deletion while importing, and persists an import record before calling the native FBX factory. Responses distinguish imported, rolled_back, partial (save failed) and outcome_unknown (record update failed). Inspect retained staging and destination state before retrying. Reusing a transfer with an import record is rejected even after rollback.

Results include asset/class identity, native geometry counts/bounds, at most 256 signed vertex positions with an explicit truncation flag, material-slot names, save status and bounded relevant native diagnostics. Without material definitions, this stage creates no material assets. It creates no actors. Native import commands are not yet exposed as standalone MCP tools or a completed transfer workflow; orchestration and downstream acceptance remain separate requirements.

Static-mesh actor placement

The existing actor recipe supports optional mesh_path on spawn operations whose class_path is /Script/Engine.StaticMeshActor. Use the exact loaded object path, for example /Game/ForgeTransfer/SM_Cube.SM_Cube; package-only paths, unloaded assets, non-static-mesh objects and non-/Game/ references are rejected. Mesh assignment is not accepted on transform/visibility operations or other actor classes. The server validates the corresponding typed recipe before dispatch.

Preview includes the intended mesh reference and transform in its changes and fingerprints the loaded mesh geometry/topology and material references. Apply consumes the actor preview and performs native component assignment inside the editor transaction. Inspection returns static_mesh, material_assets, material_assets_truncated, bounds_origin and bounds_extent on StaticMeshActor results. Location and bounds use centimeters; rotation is pitch/yaw/roll in degrees. Successful placement leaves the level unsaved. Material references describe what is assigned in Unreal; they do not establish that Blender material assets transferred.

Actor deletion is a separate one-actor unreal_preview_actor_delete / unreal_apply_actor_delete operation. Preview binds the exact loaded actor, class, world and state; world infrastructure, attached actors, actors with attached children, and actors outside the active level are rejected. Apply uses Unreal's editor destroy path inside an undo transaction. It does not save the map; Ctrl+Z remains available until a separate current-level save is applied.

Constant-PBR material transfer

Exported material slots may carry a surface classification. pbr_constants contains three bounded scene-linear base-color components, roughness and metallic in 0..1, and a strict Boolean two_sided. unsupported identifies shader graphs, transparency, non-default BSDF features, animation or out-of-range values. Missing/unsupported profiles are rejected when the server staging helper is called with transfer_materials=True. Geometry-only staging remains a separate explicit mode and does not claim material transfer.

The native import recipe optionally includes material_definitions, with at most 32 entries subject to the existing 16 KiB request limit. Each entry has exactly index, source_name, asset_path, color_space, base_color, roughness, metallic and two_sided. Indices must be ordered and contiguous; source names must be unique. color_space must be scene_linear. Package destinations must match <mesh-package-folder>/M_<transfer_id>_<index> and must not already exist. All fields require exact JSON types, and all constants must be finite and bounded.

Preview reports the new material destinations. After FBX import, native slot names and counts must match the definitions before any material is created. The importer constructs opaque Default Lit constant graphs, sets sidedness, assigns them to the mesh and saves materials before saving the mesh when save=True. A material save failure leaves a partial result and prevents mesh save; materials and saved_assets identify individual outcomes. Recovery records retain planned package destinations before import starts.

Native material results report constants read from actual expressions, native_graph_verified, individual saved status and shader_compile_verified: false. Matching parameters and saved packages do not establish shader compilation or identical appearance across renderers. Advanced graphs, textures, transparency and animated materials require further workflows.

Durable transfer receipts

forge_inspect_transfer accepts a 32-character lowercase hexadecimal operation ID and reads its private receipt under the configured project root's Saved/ForgeWorkflows/<operation_id>/record.json. It accepts no caller-selected filesystem path. Missing, malformed, linked or oversized records return explicit errors. Recorded completion is not a fresh application-state verification.

The receipt store orders export, staging, import, verification and optional placement. A started receipt must precede a native side effect; completion evidence must be persisted after the native reply. Revisions prevent stale writers and an OS file lock excludes concurrent writers. A crashed process releases its lock; the mere presence of record.lock never establishes a running operation.

After restart, an unfinished started step reports effective_state: outcome_unknown. A completed step followed by an interrupted coordinator reports interrupted. Every inspection includes runtime_state_verified: false and automatic_native_replay_allowed: false. Native reconciliation/recovery remains a separate requirement. Known credential fields, nonfinite data, excessive nesting and records above 256 KiB are rejected. Receipt inspection performs no mutation.

Connected transfer MCP tools

forge_preview_transfer(request) requires explicit source/target session IDs, source object and a new /Game/ asset destination. Optional fields control asset saving, placement and its location/rotation/scale. Both adapters must report transfer_contract_version: 1. Preview checks native identity, supported constant PBR materials and destination availability without writing transfer artifacts. It returns an operation/preview ID with a 300-second lifetime.

forge_apply_transfer(preview_id, confirmation) consumes the matching preview once and connects export, staging, import, verification and optional placement. Receipt writes precede native side effects. Native timeouts stop with an unknown outcome; the coordinator does not automatically retry native mutations. Completed verification compares bounds/counts and, for meshes of at most 256 vertices, complete signed vertex positions. It verifies constant material graphs and native actor references/transform. It does not verify shaders or rendered appearance and does not save the level. Existing asset destinations are rejected.

Loaded static-mesh inspection

unreal_inspect_static_mesh(asset_path, session_id) invokes native mesh_info for an exact loaded /Game/ mesh object. Unknown fields and mismatched object/package names are rejected. It performs no asset loads or writes. Inspection is bounded to 100000 vertices, 200000 triangles, 32 material slots and 256 sampled positions. It reports geometry, available constant material graphs, package dirty flags and disk-package presence with runtime_state_verified: true. This verifies current loaded state; disk existence is explicitly weaker than saved-content verification. A missing loaded object returns mesh_not_loaded, rather than reimporting it.

forge_reconcile_transfer(operation_id, target_session_id) reads the retained receipt and verifies the explicitly selected Unreal project's identity before native mesh inspection. It compares loaded geometry and constant material graphs with completed export evidence where available. It reports recorded state and current observations separately; receipts remain unchanged and recovery remains incomplete. When a mesh is not loaded, registry inspection supplies limited evidence without loading or reimporting. Actor placement and saved disk contents require separate verification.

Evaluated Blender rig inspection

blender_inspect_rig accepts optional include_evaluated: true in addition to weight inspection. It reports the current frame and native evaluated bone matrices in armature/world space, plus world head/tail positions. It never changes the scene frame. Evaluated inspection requires the active view layer and at most 256 bones; nonfinite results are rejected. These measurements describe evaluated application state, not proof of visible playback or rendered animation.

Adapter 0.2.4 also returns evaluated_meshes_included and an evaluated_mesh entry for each related mesh when evaluation is requested. The entry contains frame, vertex_count, face_count, world_vertices, vertices_truncated, world_bounds_min, world_bounds_max, coordinate_space: blender_world, includes_modifier_stack: true and vertex_indices_match_source: false. Empty meshes have null bounds. Sampling is limited to 256 positions per mesh; bounds cover every evaluated vertex. Queries allow at most 32 related meshes and 100000 total evaluated vertices, and reject related meshes outside the active view layer. Temporary evaluated mesh data is cleared even if inspection fails.

Retained-export asset recovery

forge_preview_asset_recovery(operation_id, target_session_id, new_asset_path) accepts eligible partial/uncertain/interrupted transfers with completed export and staging evidence. It requires the recorded Unreal project and a different, absent destination. Retained binary FBX integrity is checked before preview and again before apply. The expiring preview binds the session token identity, project/level, source receipt revision and artifact metadata. No live Blender session is required.

forge_apply_asset_recovery(preview_id, confirmation) consumes that preview once, creates a separate recovery receipt and stages a copy under a new transfer ID. Native import and geometry/material verification follow, with new asset saves. Recovery receipts use ordered staging, import, verification stages; they do not claim a new Blender export. Original receipts, backups and partial assets are preserved. Existing destinations are protected. Partial/unknown results stop without automatic replay. This restores assets only, without placement or level save; disk-content reopening and rendered checks remain separate acceptance.

Eligible incomplete recovery receipts can also be selected as the origin of a new reviewed recovery. Their completed staging evidence is required; retained export metadata must identify that recovery operation's own transfer ID. Integrity checks use its staged artifact, rather than silently falling back to an earlier backup. Each recovery keeps a direct original_operation_id link to its selected origin. Earlier receipts and partial assets remain untouched; every attempt requires a fresh preview and different absent destination. This does not automatically retry or discard the earlier operation.

Reviewed Unreal level save

unreal_preview_level_save(asset_path, session_id) proposes saving the current single persistent editor world to a new /Game/ map. The destination must be in an absent folder so existing maps and companion files are protected. Win64 path checks reject reparse ancestors and reserved names. Preview snapshots nontransient properties of bounded world-package objects, binds world identity, expires after 300 seconds and reports that saving may change current world identity. Saving a copy of an already loaded map can leave the source world open; apply reports the actual post-save editor world and whether it changed. PIE, streaming/world-partition levels and external packages are unsupported.

unreal_apply_level_save(preview_id, confirmation, session_id) consumes the preview once, repeats state/destination checks and exclusively reserves its destination folder before calling native UEditorLoadingAndSavingUtils::SaveMap. Intent and result JSON records use temporary-file replacement under Saved/ForgeLevelSaves/<operation_id>/record.json. No referenced mesh/material assets are saved by this operation. Inspect state separately from transport ok: saved, partial and outcome_unknown are explicit; failed result recording leaves uncertainty and does not trigger a replay. Rollback and reopen are not claimed by apply. These native records do not yet have the server receipt store's OS-lock, fsync and reconciliation guarantees; native save failures and abrupt interruption require further acceptance.

The MCP server now adds a private durable level_save receipt under Saved/ForgeWorkflows/<operation_id> before requesting native save. Public receipt IDs are lowercase; native_operation_id preserves the bridge's original GUID. Preview binds the target session identity and project/world. Started/completed events use the receipt store's OS lock, fsync and atomic replacement guarantees; unfinished native intents are uncertain after restart. A failed started write prevents the native request, and a failed completion write does not trigger replay. forge_inspect_transfer also reads these level-save receipts without changing or replaying them. Recorded saving does not prove current world state or disk contents.

unreal_reconcile_level_save(operation_id, session_id) verifies the selected project, observes current world identity and reads only the map path derived from the receipt's /Game/ destination. The bounded read rejects links/reparse paths, hardlinks, oversized files and changes during reading. Successful saves retain map size/SHA256 evidence; reconciliation compares current bytes where that evidence exists. Earlier receipts without checksums and uncertain saves report no checksum comparison. File absence never resolves an unknown native operation automatically. Reconciliation does not load/save/replay maps, change receipts, infer native map contents from bytes, inspect unsaved world changes or claim completed recovery.

The existing-map operation is unreal_preview_current_level_save(session_id) / unreal_apply_current_level_save(preview_id, confirmation, session_id). It targets the active persistent level and uses Unreal's native current-level save path, which saves the level package and its loaded external-object packages (including loaded World Partition actors) without saving unrelated dirty content assets. Preview binds the exact world, level and loaded package state. Apply creates and verifies binary backups for every package that Unreal will save, calls FEditorFileUtils::SaveCurrentLevel, then reports each saved package's size and SHA-1. A detected failure restores existing package files or removes newly created package files; an incomplete rollback reports partial_backup_retained. Backups and native/server receipts remain under project Saved for inspection. This does not save unloaded World Partition actors or establish that the map has been reopened or visually tested.

Level-save previews now scan the loaded hard-reference graph of persistent world objects, bounded to 20000 queued objects, 10000 references per object and 256 external packages. Package dirty flags and disk-package presence are reported. Dirty/missing packages block preview without creating a preview ID or receipt; apply repeats the scan and rejects a dependency becoming unsaved after preview. Referenced transient material/render assets are also considered unpreserved. The operation never saves these dependencies automatically. Limits fail explicitly instead of returning a truncated successful inspection. The server requires these dependency fields and rejects older adapters without the guard.

Responses explicitly identify dependency_scan_scope: loaded_hard_references, soft_references_verified: false and dependency_saved_contents_verified: false. This guard does not establish unloaded soft-reference coverage, native saved contents or rendered equivalence. Those remain separate completion requirements.

Reviewed Blender skin binding

Adapter 0.2.5 supports bind_mesh through scene preview/apply. Required fields are source (existing mesh), armature (existing rig), name (new output), and weights: explicit {vertex, bone, weight} assignments. Every vertex must be covered with a normalized sum (tolerance 1e-5) and at most four deform-bone influences. Assignments must be unique, finite and positive; missing bones, existing output names and singular transforms are rejected. Limits are 128 vertices/faces, 64 bones and 512 assignments, also subject to the 16 KiB bridge request limit. Optional collection must name an existing collection.

The input must be a local unbound static mesh without parenting, modifiers, constraints, shape keys, animation or vertex groups. Both objects must be in the active view layer in Object mode. Mesh attributes are bounded; string attributes are unsupported. The output has independent mesh data, native vertex groups and an Armature modifier using those groups, with bone envelopes disabled. Native weight assignments are verified before completion is reported. The original is preserved; the scene remains unsaved. Preview binds source geometry/attributes and rig rest/pose/transform facts. Failure uses the existing rollback/partial contract. This describes the initial 0.2.5 binding profile.

Adapter 0.2.6 adds reweight_mesh with the same explicit normalized weight contract and limits. The source must already have exactly one enabled Armature modifier using vertex groups on the specified rig. Parenting may be absent or object-parenting to that same rig. Bone envelopes, masks, multiple-modifier skinning, non-bone groups and other modifier types are rejected. The reviewed new copy replaces its copied bone groups/weights while preserving original skin data, parenting/world transforms and the preserve-volume setting. Preview also fingerprints original weights, group definitions and parent facts. Failure removes only new datablocks. In-place changes, automatic weights and skeletal transfer remain outside this profile.

With include_weights, rig inspection now includes vertex_weight_samples (vertex, weights: [{bone, weight}]) for the first 128 source vertices and up to 512 bone assignments per related mesh. vertex_weight_samples_truncated explicitly identifies incomplete samples. Aggregate statistics still cover the full bounded scan. Supported skin-copy workflows fit the full sample bounds.

Adapter 0.2.7 adds auto_bind_mesh with required source, armature, new name and weight_method: blender_heat_top4; explicit weights are not accepted for this method. The native Blender ARMATURE_AUTO solver runs only after apply, on a new independent mesh copy. Its results are limited to the strongest four deform-bone influences per vertex and normalized, then actual native assignments are verified. Unweighted vertices, invalid solver output or operator failure yield the bounded automatic_weights_failed code and batch rollback/partial status. Source objects, selection and active object are preserved. Preview exposes the algorithm, not already-computed weights; apply marks requires_deformation_review: true.

Automatic binding supports up to 10000 source vertices, 20000 faces and 64 bones, on an unbound local static mesh with the same source/context restrictions as explicit binding. Mesh attribute data remains bounded. Rig rest/pose, transforms, bone envelope/radius facts and source geometry/attributes participate in preview binding. It is a native solver starting point, not a promise of production-quality deformation on arbitrary characters. Skeletal transfer and general control-rig workflows remain separate requirements.

Reviewed Blender positional IK profile (adapter 0.2.10)

Use scene preview/apply to create an Empty control (create_empty, with name, optional location/rotation/scale/collection). A subsequent reviewed operation uses:

{"op":"create_ik_constraint","name":"CharacterRig","ik":{"bone":"Forearm","constraint":"ForgeArmIK","target":"HandControl","chain_count":2,"iterations":128}}

Names in the IK spec use bounded ASCII identifiers. Chain count is explicitly 1..16; iterations are 1..256 (default 64). The native profile uses tail position, full influence, no stretching and no rotation target. It requires an existing local rig (at most 64 bones), an unconstrained chain and existing Empty target. Both objects must be unparented, in Object mode and the active view layer, without object constraints/drivers/NLA. Only one IK creation is allowed per batch. Preview is single-use and fingerprints rig/target state. Rollback removes the newly created constraint; existing constraints are not overwritten. Results require deformation review. Inspect evaluated rig output to measure the actual result, including unreachable target behavior. Pole-target setup and constraint revisions are not implemented by this profile.

Adapter 0.2.11 extends the positional IK spec with optional pole_target (a distinct existing Empty) and pole_angle (finite radians within +/-pi, default zero). A pole requires at least two bones and a non-collinear bend plane. Its identity/transform and Action are included in preview fingerprints. IK apply reports evaluated tail and target positions, target_distance_world, position_tolerance_world (0.0001), target_reached, frame and warning code ik_target_not_reached when outside tolerance. Creation success verifies the constraint setup; clients must review the measured convergence, especially for straight rest chains or unreachable targets.

Reviewed existing DataAsset edits — Unreal adapter 0.2.8 / MCP server 0.3.1

unreal_preview_data_asset_edit and unreal_apply_data_asset_edit edit an existing, loaded DataAsset with a bounded set of 1–32 editable simple reflected properties. Preview identifies the asset, requested values, current values and exact confirmation; apply requires that confirmation and rejects expired, reused, stale, dirty or identity- changed targets. Asset paths are restricted to /Game and /JasperPrism. Saving is explicit. Before a save, the adapter preserves and verifies a copy of the original package under the project's Saved area, then reads back applied values. Native FBoolProperty accessors are used for bitfield booleans. Arrays, nested containers, and object/asset references are excluded from this profile. Receipts report applied values, save status and backup metadata; a receipt does not imply visual/runtime QA.
